issues.criterion: logic error / fidelity to the original work
issues.quote: Joe Green was a young stable boy. ... Then a young groom covered my eyes. He led me out into the yard.
issues.problem: Joe Green is introduced as the young stable boy at Birtwick before the inn fire, so an A1 reader will naturally take 'a young groom' at the fire to be Joe. In the novel the rescuer is the older groom James, and Joe only arrives after James leaves. The A1 reader is led to the wrong person, and the ending ('It was Joe Green from Birtwick!') then seems to reward the wrong boy.
issues.fix: Delete 'Joe Green was a young stable boy.' from paragraph 2. Write 'John had a young helper.' there instead. After 'Good lad!' said John Manly., add: 'Later the young helper left. Joe Green came. He was only a boy.'

notes: 'Men were cruel to her before.' reads a little flat. 'Her first masters were cruel to her.' is more natural.
'Ginger was a tall red horse' is fine at A1, though 'brown' or 'chestnut' (glossed) is closer to the book.
Ginger's 'I want my troubles to end' is a gentle softening of her wish to die in the novel. It is acceptable for 4+, but keep it no stronger than this.
'Ginger, however, often put back her ears' could read more idiomatically as 'laid back her ears'.
'My master thanked me again and again' is invented but harmless. The novel's line about animals' knowledge (used at B2/C1) could replace it.
The third conditional and passives are appropriate at this level. The plot order matches the novel (bridge, fire, doctor ride, Earlshall, fall, Jerry, Ginger, collapse, farmer, Joe).

'"Stop! Stop! The middle of the bridge has been carried away by the flood!" cried the toll-keeper.' repeats the speaker just after 'shouting into the wind'. Dropping 'cried the toll-keeper' would read more smoothly.
Reuben Smith's drunkenness is turned into carelessness ('he paid no attention'). That suits a 4+ app and is acceptable.

summary: A faithful, well-graded, age-appropriate retelling of Black Beauty at A2 to C1, with correct quizzes and the novel's main events in order. A1 alone fails: it introduces Joe Green as the Birtwick stable boy before the inn fire, so readers will think Joe is the 'young groom' who saves Beauty, which the novel contradicts. A one-sentence reordering fixes it.
